matcher_index_reproducible.why_the_unit_is_not_pedantry: RESOLVED, and both numbers were right: the coordinator's 217870 is in PYTHON CODE POINTS, mine is in UTF-16 CODE UNITS. I verified his explanation myself rather than accept it - in Python the brace sits at 217870, in JS at 217871 with a space at 217870, and encoding the prefix up to the Python index gives exactly 217871 UTF-16 units. The cause is one astral character before the dictionary anchor: U+1F4C1 FILE FOLDER at Python code point 89215, which JS counts as TWO units. MINE IS THE NUMBER THAT BEARS ON THE PREDICATE, because the harness runs in node and the assert is about a JS string index - his was a correct measurement of a different unit. REFINEMENT I measured on top of his finding: the offset is POSITION-DEPENDENT, not a constant +1. The file holds 55 astral characters in total but only ONE before this anchor, so the JS-Python gap is +1 at this position and grows to +55 by end of file - the whole-file lengths differ by exactly 55 (JS 1091026 vs Python 1090971), which confirms it. A reader probing a LATER position with a Python tool would see a different offset again, so naming the unit matters more than the single number does.
